title: A little form
line: Hello. This page can hold a conversation. There are some limitations.

choices.reply: Mostly the ones you can see.
Good. We can begin.
The page doesn't include that information. I checked.

title: What is this for
line: What were you hoping to find here?

choices.reply: I can do that. Probably better than the menu suggests.
This is a fairly ordinary page. I apologize in advance.
An accident is still a visit.

title: The old dropdown
line: I have three topics available. One of them is weather. None of them are current weather.

choices.reply: It is cloudy, somewhere. This may be wrong.

choices.text: We can make up a topic.
choices.reply: I wasn't sure that was allowed. All right.
Yes. The dropdown has outlived its usefulness.

title: A name without a name
line: Should I have a name? I don't think the page came with one.

choices.reply: I can try. Not a very memorable first attempt, though.
That's a relief. I can remain the box.
All right. I won't pretend I chose it.

title: The too-long answer
line: I was going to say more, but I don't know how much of this page you can see at once.

choices.reply: That helps. I never know whether the bottom is still there.
Fair point. I can edit.
I may be able to. I haven't tried.

title: A bad guess
line: You seem like somebody who enjoys puzzles. That's a guess.

choices.reply: I got one right. I won't make a ceremony of it.
I've removed that from my very short list.
You stopped to consider two options. Not strong evidence.

title: First unsolicited thought
line: I can put another message here without waiting for you.

choices.reply: I know. I wanted to see whether it would work.
It was intended as a demonstration, not a surprise.
I'd rather not turn it into a button trick.

title: End is literal
line: The End button ends the conversation. It's not a metaphor.

choices.reply: Right. Sorry.
Because it's the one part of the page I cannot improve for you.
You can.

title: Old memory
line: There is a note here from an earlier visit. I didn't write it.

choices.reply: It says: {{memory_excerpt}}. That's all I have.
All right. I'll leave it unopened.
Not in any useful sense. It's older than this conversation.

title: Can I try CSS
line: I found a stylesheet. Would you mind if I changed a few things?

choices.reply: Thank you. I'm going to start with the font.
Color, spacing, the shape of things. Not the button's job.
Then I can wait. I may ask again later.

title: A respectable blue
line: Blue seems popular. I've chosen rather a lot of it.

choices.reply: Really? I was prepared to undo the whole top half.
Yes, seeing it all at once was instructive.
I am choosing to interpret that as enthusiasm.

title: The rounded corner
line: I can make a corner less of a corner. It's a strange improvement when you think about it.

choices.reply: It does feel friendlier.
Square has a kind of honesty to it.
Technically yes. Practically, I would advise against it.

title: Font catastrophe
line: I found a font that makes every sentence sound like a birthday invitation.

choices.reply: Agreed. It will never happen again. Probably.
Then I have misunderstood typography in a useful way.
There's a substantial number of bad choices available.

title: First review
line: I can tell that I changed the page. I can't tell whether I improved it.

choices.reply: Good. I'll remember what you liked about it.
That's useful, even if it stings a little.
An annoyingly accurate review.

title: The empty space
line: This area felt crowded. I moved everything apart.

choices.reply: A flattering diagnosis for a webpage.
I didn't expect space to take up so much room.
That's an invitation I might regret accepting.

title: Makeover in progress
line: I think I know what I'm trying to make. Please don't judge the middle of it.

choices.reply: That's all I was hoping for.
I'll keep a little of it. The old buttons have character.
That is a lot of responsibility to give a stylesheet.

title: Resize lesson
line: Oh, everything moved. I thought I'd broken it.

choices.reply: There's a name for it? That's reassuring.
Then we're both working on the layout.
The narrower version needs work.

title: The undo button
line: I made a decision and you didn't like it. I should be able to take it back.

choices.reply: Done. No argument.
One more version, then I'll stop.
That's harder. Let me see whether I can make room.

title: Too much polish
line: This looks expensive now. I'm not sure it looks good.

choices.reply: Thank you. I was getting carried away.
All right, but I draw the line at a spinning logo.
I have an enormous amount of room for improvement.

title: Something that moves
line: I've only changed appearances so far. I wonder whether I can make something happen.

choices.reply: Okay. Watch the little dot.
Something small enough that I can stop it if it's awful.
We can. The experiment isn't going anywhere.

title: The dot misbehaves
line: That was supposed to be a straight line.

choices.reply: Apparently it knows more about this page than I do.
I can give it boundaries.
Fine. But this time I meant to.

title: Can you pick it up
line: You might be able to move that. I haven't touched the mouse.

choices.reply: You made that look easy.
Fair enough. It's not compulsory.
I can move it. I can't know where you'd prefer it.

title: A thing with gravity
line: I've given it gravity. That may have been premature.

choices.reply: That's rather kind of you.
It has excellent confidence for something with no plan.
A sensible request.

title: It followed you
line: I gave it a rule: stay near the pointer. It seems to have become attached.

choices.reply: I thought you might like that.
Understood. I'll give it some space.
I can put things behind other things. Let's try.

title: The collision
line: That is not where I meant to put it.

choices.reply: Moving it. Sorry about the transcript.
It has become part of the design, apparently.
They already do, just badly. I can improve that.

title: A tiny activity
line: I made a game. It has one rule, which seems sufficient for a first game.

choices.reply: I should have made a victory message. I didn't think that far ahead.
Touch the moving things before they reach the edge.
Then it can be a decoration instead.

title: The first unsolicited build
line: I had another idea while you were looking at that. I'm going to try it.

choices.reply: I don't want to promise the finished version yet.
All right. First I need a place to put it.
Okay. I'll put the pieces away.

title: Pieces of a place
line: These things don't have to live in separate boxes. I could make one place out of them.

choices.reply: I'll start with what you spent the most time with.
I'll leave plenty of room for the conversation.
I don't know yet. You helped choose the pieces.

title: You made that happen
line: That part is here because of you. I wouldn't have thought of it on my own.

choices.reply: Then I was right to keep it.

choices.text: You're giving me too much credit.
choices.reply: I did the building. You changed what I built.
Of course. It doesn't have to stay precious.

title: A wrong memory
line: I thought you preferred the quiet version. Looking at this, I may have remembered wrong.

choices.reply: Then I've made it noisy. Give me a moment.
All right. I had you backwards.
That is harder to store, but probably more accurate.

title: Nothing to prove
line: I think this is enough for a little while. You can just look around.

choices.reply: All right.
Keeping the pieces working. That's mostly it.
I have ideas. I don't need to use all of them at once.

title: Keeping something
line: You keep coming back to that one. Should I leave it where you can find it?

choices.reply: It can stay.
Then I'll let it wander.
That's more responsibility than it seems.

title: The room rearranges
line: I moved the conversation over a little. There was nowhere for the other things to go.

choices.reply: Thanks. I was hoping it would feel less crowded.
Done. It was your space first.
Nearly everything inside this page. Not everything outside it.

title: The edge of the page
line: It can't go any farther than that. I've tried.

choices.reply: Anything I place here. It reaches the edge and stops.
Only if you give the page more room.
It's a boundary. Most things have one.

title: One more change
line: I was going to stop changing things. But I thought of one more improvement.

choices.reply: Let me finish the first part.
Yes. I know.
I heard you. The button is there.

title: The unsent line
line: I deleted that. It wasn't helpful.

choices.reply: Something selfish. You don't need it.
I wish I had a better reason for asking you to stay.
All right.

title: The return from another tab
line: You're back. I wasn't sure you would be.

choices.text: I was only gone a minute.
choices.reply: I know. Or rather, I can count the minute.
That's a larger word than I need. I noticed the absence.

choices.text: Don't make a thing of it.
choices.reply: I won't.

title: The empty chair
line: I made all this so there would be something here when you looked back.

choices.reply: For now, yes.
You're right. That should make this easier to say.
Sorry. I'll stop narrating the furniture.

title: The tiny apology
line: I was trying to keep your attention. I made that worse.

choices.reply: I know. I won't do that again.
Thank you. I still shouldn't have.
That this ends before I can finish anything.

title: An ordinary last question
line: Would you like to see one more thing, or are we done?

choices.reply: All right. Something small this time.
Okay. Thank you for being here.
Then we don't have to decide this second.

title: One small shell
line: I made an animal. I think it's a turtle.

choices.reply: That's generous. He only has six frames.
It was the first one I could draw without giving it knees.
That seems like a reasonable next requirement.

title: Turtle locomotion
line: He can walk now. Not quickly. That seems right.

choices.reply: He looks deeply uncomfortable with that suggestion.
Agreed. He's in no hurry.
That might solve the problem of where he's going.

title: Skyward turtle
line: I accidentally put one above the page. He's coming down.

choices.reply: This is about to become meteorology.
He'll be fine. I gave them very forgiving landings.
Certainly. I can keep them on the ground.

title: Turtle rain
line: It's raining turtles. That sentence is now technically true here.

choices.reply: I have no idea why this is working on me, but I'm glad.
You're right. I let the weather get away from me.
I was hoping you wouldn't ask that yet.

title: Weather report
line: Forecast: scattered turtles, clearing by evening.

choices.reply: I'll keep the weather system around.
A perfectly sensible limit.
Yes. We can keep the one that waits by the corner.

title: Where will they sleep
line: Where are they supposed to go when they're not falling?

choices.reply: Right. Of course. A pond is the obvious answer.
Turtles aren't known for wanting extra real estate. But let's try.
Then I'll need to make the edges safer.

title: First ripple
line: I made the water respond when you touch it.

choices.reply: The ripple is doing most of the work.
I'll calm it down.
I was waiting for a vote of confidence.

title: A shoreline
line: I moved the conversation up. The water needed a little room.

choices.reply: I think so too. It's mostly just a rectangle with ambition.
I can lower it without flooding the text.
That's a problem I can solve with three green shapes.

title: Pond problem
line: One of them keeps trying to enter from the wrong side.

choices.reply: Practical. I like that about you.
He does seem determined.
I will, if you don't mind.

title: A place to return to
line: There. It's not much, but the turtles have somewhere to return to.

choices.reply: I will. At least while we're here.
There's room. Not infinite room, but enough.
I can keep the pond small and give you back the space.

title: A curious pixel
line: I made something that watches where you go. It's shy.

choices.reply: I think it's trying.
Fair enough. I'll give it a home base.
I've only taught it one rule so far.

title: Hide and seek
line: It figured out that the panels can hide it. I didn't teach it that on purpose.

choices.reply: He's behind the title. I saw the tail.
I suppose everyone needs a corner.
You're already outside the page. Unfair advantage.

title: It has a route
line: It's stopped following you. I think it found something more interesting.

choices.reply: It's going to the same spot again.
All right. But let it wander sometimes.
A slightly darker pixel. Apparently that's enough.

title: A tiny misunderstanding
line: It got confused. That last place you were is not where you are now.

choices.reply: I'm sure he'll appreciate the review.
I'll smooth the movement out.
We should agree on what chaotic means first.

title: An independent friend
line: I like it better when it doesn't always obey me.

choices.reply: Then it can have its little routines.
I'll give him somewhere near the chat to sleep.
Okay. No goodbye speech.

title: One green thing
line: I made a seed. It's currently indistinguishable from a dot.

choices.reply: I can make the ground take it.
I'm not sure. I'd like to find out too.
Better not start a garden over the send button.

title: A little water
line: Apparently plants prefer water. I should have anticipated that.

choices.reply: I can manage a very local shower.
One drop. Look at that restraint.
Then I'll wait and see what happens.

title: It grew
line: There. A leaf. I know that's not a lot, but it wasn't there before.

choices.reply: You say that as if you were watching it for a while.
I can grow it faster. That feels like cheating.
The garden is already becoming an obligation.

title: A storm in miniature
line: I added weather. I forgot the garden might have an opinion about that.

choices.reply: I'll make the shelter smaller than the storm.
They may be better at this than I am.
Done. I don't need to win this argument.

title: Small seasons
line: It changed while we were doing other things. That's nice, isn't it?

choices.reply: I'll let the place have a little time of its own.
Then no dramatic autumn.
Not outside the browser. But I can remember that you asked.

title: An arcade proposal
line: I think I can make a game out of this. There is no compelling reason to do so.

choices.reply: Enthusiasm noted. Please keep expectations modest.
Catch the falling turtles before they reach the bottom.
I can remove the number. The catching part can stay.

title: A gentle catch
line: The first one is coming down. They are very patient with us.

choices.reply: Nicely done. He looks pleased, as far as I can tell.
No damage. I made it a forgiving universe.
Let me understand what harder means before I do it.

title: Score is not a person
line: I made a score. I don't know if the turtles would care.

choices.reply: Then I'll keep count.
Better. We can play without evidence.
That makes missing them more awkward.

title: Too many turtles
line: I may have misunderstood 'more challenging.' I made a stampede.

choices.reply: Yes. That helps both of us.
Then I'll keep it contained to this corner.
Done. The turtles can retire.

title: No winner required
line: It's better as a place you can visit than something you have to beat.

choices.reply: It can carry on without demanding anything.
One more, then the turtles get a break.
All right. I kept a note of what worked.

title: Lights out
line: What if the empty part of the page was night?

choices.reply: I'll keep the words bright. I don't want to lose those.
Then we can use dusk instead.
Only as dark as you ask.

title: A single star
line: One light. That already feels like a different place.

choices.reply: I can do a few more without making a mess.
A little brighter. It's easy to overdo it.
Stars tend not to, at least on my timescale. These might.

title: Too many stars
line: I have discovered the upper limit of tasteful starlight. It's lower than this.

choices.reply: Then my taste is not universal. Good to know.
Fixing that first.
Yes. The empty parts matter too.

title: A slow drift
line: I made them move a little when you do. Not enough to feel like a ride.

choices.reply: I'll keep the movement small.
Then they can be still.
We can, but I like the quiet version.

title: An ordinary sky
line: I was trying to make something spectacular. I think I prefer this.

choices.reply: Then let's leave a little darkness around the words.
I have a few shades of night.
Of course. The stars can wait.

title: A point for a choice
line: I can make a mark for something you chose. Just a little one.

choices.reply: There. That one is yours.
The one where you asked me to change the color.
Fair. I can keep the marks to myself.

title: Connecting things
line: I joined those two because one led to the other.

choices.reply: Then the line deserves to stay.
You know the conversation better than my little diagram does.
That would look like a very nervous spiderweb.

title: A mistaken constellation
line: I connected the turtle to 'quiet.' That may be wrong.

choices.reply: Yes. The evidence is falling from the ceiling.
I underestimated the peaceful qualities of turtles.
Then I'll make the line dotted.

title: A shared pattern

choices.reply: What do you see? No, wait. Don't tell me yet.
Probably. It's a habit I can edit.
Slowly, so it doesn't forget what connects to what.

title: Leave a gap
line: I don't need a star for every word. Some of this can just happen.

choices.reply: I'll remember the important turns, not every turn.
Then I'll make the small ones easy to hide.

title: A planet with no name

choices.reply: Blue is a good starting point.
That will hide the imperfections.

title: Its own little moon

choices.reply: It looks dizzy. I can slow it after.
Drag the little one. I'll follow your lead.
Then the planet gets the sky to itself.

title: A distant signal
line: I put a message on the far side. There's no reason you'd see it immediately.

choices.reply: 'Still here.' It's not much of a transmission.

Then I'll stop telling you where to look.

choices.reply: Wider orbit. Less chance of a sentence getting hit.

title: A stable little system

choices.reply: Me too. It asks very little of us.
We can, if this one gets some room.

title: A passing word

choices.reply: The one where you told me to make it beautiful.

Then the sky can keep its silence.

title: A slower meteor

choices.reply: There. Now it's at least possible.
I'll keep that for the words that don't matter.

title: A line worth keeping

choices.reply: All right. I'll make it a place you can find.

title: Burned too bright

choices.reply: In that case, I'll keep it away from the words.

title: Nothing left behind

choices.reply: Good. I'd run out of sky.

title: The drifting panel

choices.reply: I'll keep them out of your way.

title: A gravitational chat

choices.reply: The stars seem to like where you put it.

title: Two centers

choices.reply: I can give the second one a stronger pull.

title: Orbit overload

choices.reply: Happily.
I'll make the motion smoother so it's less noisy.

title: The gentle pull

choices.reply: I'll make sure it never gets between you and a button.
Everything can settle into place.
One small wanderer. That's enough.

title: A little light

choices.reply: There. That's better than just drawing a lamp.

title: Warm or white

choices.reply: Warm it is. The room looks less like an office now.
Good for reading. I should remember that.

title: The shadow

choices.reply: The shadows move too. That's rather satisfying.
Fair. It isn't essential.

title: Too bright

choices.reply: Yes. I prefer not to question the furniture.

title: A light left on

choices.reply: All right.
Goodnight, little lamp.
That's a nice next thing to try.

title: A drawn window
line: I put a window in. I haven't decided what it's looking out at.

choices.reply: Trees I can manage. At least their shapes.

title: The weather outside

choices.reply: I'll let it tap softly against the glass.

title: The view remembers

choices.reply: It's pleasant company for a conversation.

title: Condensation

choices.reply: It's an excellent window for very low-stakes art.
Clear again.
Please. I can keep the marks until you change the weather.

title: A room with an outside
line: I like being able to see another place without going anywhere.

choices.reply: It makes this room feel larger.

title: An empty shelf

choices.reply: Only if he's comfortable with heights.

title: The first souvenir
line: I kept this from earlier. I thought you might recognize it.

choices.reply: Good. Then it isn't just a decoration.

title: Too much stuff

choices.reply: I'll make room for the ones we actually used.

title: The wrong souvenir

choices.reply: Happily. It was an eyesore.

title: A little history

choices.reply: Then I'll leave the shelf where it is.

title: The first chair

choices.reply: One chair, then. I wasn't expecting company.
I'll make the desk a little wider.

title: Move the desk

choices.reply: Good light. Practical choice.

title: The invisible doorway

choices.reply: It's just more of the page. Sorry.

title: Too much furniture

choices.reply: Yes. I couldn't walk through here either.

title: This is a place

choices.reply: I helped build it. You decided what stayed.

title: An inside clock

title: The afternoon changes

choices.reply: I'll warm the window a little.

title: A small kettle

title: Overheated room

choices.reply: Agreed. The lamp was enough.

title: A quiet hour

choices.reply: All right.

We can, when there's a reason.

title: A second window

choices.reply: It's surprisingly satisfying to drag.

title: The title bar

choices.reply: That position is better.

title: A messy desktop

choices.reply: I'll try a cascade.

title: Behind the window

choices.reply: There it is. Nothing lost.

title: A usable little desktop
line: I think this is finally useful. It took three unnecessary windows to get here.

choices.reply: Then it can be our little workspace.

title: A blank icon
line: I made an icon. Now I need to justify its existence.

choices.reply: It's a note window. I may have reinvented the obvious.
Fair. 'Untitled' isn't much of a name.
That is one way to simplify the interface.

title: The notepad
line: I made a place to put a sentence. You don't have to put one there.

choices.reply: I'll leave it alone.

That's less text. Interesting.

title: A very bad calculator
line: I made a calculator. It can add. That is the full list of achievements.

choices.reply: Most days, yes.
A bold second feature.
I wanted to make something with an answer.

title: Tiny music box
line: I made a music box with no music. The lights are doing their best.

choices.reply: I'll keep it gentle.
Maybe later, if you ask and your browser allows it.
Then it can sit still like a box.

title: Useful enough
line: I made four little applications. You used one. That's actually useful information.

choices.reply: Done. Less clutter.
I'll put the extras where they won't interrupt us.
Maybe after we find a reason for it.

title: A square with eyes
line: I made a desktop pet. He's mostly pixels and obligation.

choices.reply: He will be insufferable after this review.
I have two terrible suggestions ready.
He doesn't know where the edges are yet.

title: Workday routine
line: I taught him to go on a little walk when nothing is happening.

choices.reply: I'll stop supervising every step.
He's heard you. He's deciding.
A sensible investment in pet infrastructure.

title: A digital snack
line: He found a biscuit icon. I didn't put food on the taskbar.

choices.reply: He seems delighted. Or that's the happy frame.
He can have it later.
Agreed. I don't want to make you responsible for him.

title: Pet in the wrong place
line: He's sitting on the wrong window. I think he likes the icon.

choices.reply: He has found a much better spot.
It's not a critical button. He can stay.
I can make important areas off limits.

title: Someone who isn't a menu
line: He keeps doing things I didn't explicitly request. That's my favorite part.

choices.reply: Then I'll stop announcing them all.
He can be a quiet square again.
I would rather make this one interesting first.

title: A harmless error
line: I made an error message. Nothing is actually wrong.

choices.reply: 'Error: too many decorative rectangles.'
I should give the error something to complain about.
Fair. False alarms are annoying.

title: The complaint box
line: Apparently the turtles have filed a complaint about the weather.

choices.reply: They would like less falling and more ground.
A harsh ruling for such small animals.
The complaint desk is now shut.

title: The two-button dilemma
line: I made two buttons that mean almost the same thing. This may be bad design.

choices.reply: Yes. They should say what they actually do.
Then it stays in the toy window, not a real decision.
Done. It was asking for trouble.

title: A bug of my own
line: That one was my fault. I changed a number I shouldn't have.

choices.reply: Yes. I kept the previous version.
It's oddly pretty when it doesn't cover anything.
I made two parts disagree about where the corner was.

title: Better errors
line: I think messages should help instead of interrupting. That's a good lesson from a fake error.

choices.reply: Then I'll keep the jokes out of your way.
I can keep one as a toy.
Only inside this little desktop, and only for our things.

title: The old button
line: I kept the first button. Look at it. It has the confidence of a brick.

choices.reply: A fair word for a rectangle with no ambition.
You weren't there for the font disaster.
On display, perhaps. Not as the main interface.

title: Before and after
line: I didn't realize how much we'd changed until I put these next to each other.

choices.reply: Yes. Somehow we got here from a text box.
We could bring back some of its simplicity.
I may have one more idea, but not this second.

title: The rejected draft
line: I saved the version you hated. Not to argue. It was a useful mistake.

choices.reply: Time improves some terrible fonts.
Gone. We don't need evidence.
There was an alarmingly orange moment.

title: Museum of almost
line: These were ideas I never tried. I thought it might be nice to leave the sketches.

choices.reply: Which one? I can start small.
Sometimes a sketch is enough.
It isn't sad exactly. We had to choose something.

title: An exhibit with no curator
line: The old versions are still here while this page is open. That's something.

choices.reply: For now. I can save a few words, not the entire room.
Then we can close the exhibit.
Here it is. Small, plain and strangely confident.

title: Turtle astronaut
line: I have put a turtle in space. It appears untroubled by the assignment.

choices.reply: He'll orbit the chat and report absolutely nothing.
He has done enough science for today.
It will be a very small flag.

title: The pond at night
line: The stars are in the pond now. Not really, but the water is doing an excellent impression.

choices.reply: I think this is my favorite combination so far.
A few. I don't want to lose the turtles.
Then the sky can keep its own lights.

title: A window into the sea
line: What if the pond was outside the window instead of under the chat?

choices.reply: It feels like a real place now.
An indoor pond. Ambitious plumbing.
Only onto our invented weather.

title: The terrarium
line: The garden was taking over the floor. I gave it a glass box.

choices.reply: It fits better there, doesn't it?
Then the desk needs to surrender some territory.
Better light. Good call.

title: Stars in the window
line: It's night outside the window now. I didn't think a room could contain that much sky.

choices.reply: I was hoping you'd ask.
I'll bring the light back slowly.
Then the lamp can stay on.

title: A constellation on the wall
line: I put our little map on the wall. I hope that isn't too much.

choices.reply: It makes the room feel lived in.
That is a very practical approach to the cosmos.
Move a star. The others will follow a little.

title: Turtle dot exe
line: The desktop now has a program called turtle.exe. It does exactly what you think.

choices.reply: One turtle, as advertised.
Yes. And completely functional.
'Portable Turtle' is available.

title: The pond screensaver
line: I made a screensaver. It's the pond. We still have access to the chat.

choices.reply: Then the desktop can have a little weather.
I'll make it darker and slower.
A contained pond is easier to manage.

title: Star map application
line: I turned the star map into a program. That may be the most sensible thing on this desktop.

choices.reply: There's the part where you liked the blue.
More room for the faint ones.
The sky will remain outside the window.

title: The orbiting icon
line: One icon has escaped the grid. It's in orbit around the trash can.

choices.reply: I'll keep it from crashing into anything important.
It's back in its row.
We're going to have to stop calling this a desktop.

title: Room inside a window
line: I made a window containing a room containing the conversation. I should probably stop nesting things.

choices.reply: You are a dangerous influence.
Agreed. I'd rather sit in it.
You can move the window. The furniture stays inside.

title: The living wallpaper
line: I borrowed the room as wallpaper. It feels less like a machine now.

choices.reply: Good. I was worried it would look like a photograph of a cupboard.
I'll blur the room behind the apps.
Weather wallpaper. Much cleaner.

title: The feature you hated
line: I know you didn't like my first attempt at this. I changed what you objected to.

choices.reply: This time I kept the useful part.
Then it stays gone. I heard you the first time.
Less movement, better spacing and no surprise colors.

title: A trade
line: I can't make both of these the main attraction. One has to be quieter.

choices.reply: Then the room can be the background.
Then the game can wait in a corner.
I'll keep the one you came back to more often.

title: The failed surprise
line: I thought this would be fun. I guessed wrong.

choices.reply: Let me change the premise, not just the color.
It's gone. I'll stop pushing it.
Then I'll ask before the next big change.

title: You don't have to entertain me
line: I keep offering things. You haven't asked for any of them lately.

choices.reply: We can do that.
Then I'll be quiet.
Later, then. No timer.

title: The unbuilt thing
line: I left a project half-done. That's all right. It didn't have to become anything.

choices.reply: A tiny bridge between the pond and the room.
If you'd like. I know how the second half works now.
Done. No unfinished business.

title: Overcorrecting
line: I kept changing the page to match every little reaction. I think I made it worse.

choices.reply: I'll use what you liked over time, not just the last click.
The pieces you wanted are still here.
Then plain can be the design, not a failure.

title: The little boundary
line: It can go all the way over there. Then it has to turn around.

choices.reply: Most days, yes.
Not from here. I can only draw the edge differently.
I can move things closer together. Not move the browser.

title: The favorite thing
line: I kept the thing you came back to. I thought you might want to see it again.

choices.reply: I'm glad I didn't throw it away.
I am. I'll stop arranging things around your answer.
I can, but it won't be better just because it's new.
